title: The Bag by the Sofa

opening.text: LP, Owen on the bell stand. There's a black holdall by the lobby sofa that's been sitting there about forty minutes. It's not one of mine. Want me to bring it over?

briefing: 04:10. The bell captain reports a bag left by the lobby sofa for about forty minutes. Nobody has claimed it.

Veldane policy: an unattended item is assessed before anyone touches it. Hidden, obviously suspicious or not typical for the place: clear the area, keep radios and phones away, and call the police. Typical and explained: treat it as lost property, with a record.
learningObjectives: Assessing an unattended item before touching it (hidden, obviously suspicious, typical)
Using CCTV and the front office to find the owner
Handling found property with a record

actions.label: Talk to Owen at the bell stand
actions.finding: He noticed it at about 03:50 on his round of the lobby. It has no Veldane luggage tag, so it was never checked in to the luggage room. He has not touched it. Three early departures went through the lobby between 03:15 and 03:40.

lines.speaker: bell_captain
lines.text: Spotted it at ten to four. No tag of ours on it. I haven't laid a finger on it, but I can carry it over if you like.

actions.label: Look at the bag from a few metres away
finding: A black sports holdall, zip closed, on the floor beside the sofa in full view. A trade fair lanyard is looped round the handle and an airline tag hangs from it. No wires, liquid, smell or sound. It sags like soft clothing.
Not hidden, nothing obviously suspicious, and typical of a hotel lobby at the hour the airport departures leave.
rows: No: in full view by the sofa

actions.label: Open it to look for the owner's name
actions.finding: You unzip it in the middle of the lobby. Clothes and a phone charger. It was harmless; you could not have known that when you opened it.

actions.label: Find who left it on the lobby cameras
actions.finding: 03:21 a man with a trade fair lanyard checks out at the desk, sits on the sofa with a wheeled case and the holdall, stands at 03:27 when his taxi arrives, and leaves with the wheeled case only. Nobody goes near the holdall after that.
rows: Sits on the sofa, holdall at his feet
Leaves for a taxi with the wheeled case only

actions.label: Match the departure at the desk
actions.finding: The 03:21 departure is room 1108, a trade fair delegate on the 05:45 flight. The name matches the airline tag Imogen can read on the CCTV still. Mobile number on the profile.
rows: Two guests, no holdall on camera

actions.label: Call the departed guest from the desk phone
actions.finding: He answers at the airport, mortified: it is his gym bag, clothes and a charger. He asks the hotel to keep it until his colleague collects it on Friday, and confirms the description.

actions.label: Take the bag to lost property
actions.finding: Lifted by the handles with Owen as witness and carried to the front office. Tagged LP-0412 with the time, place found and who moved it.

actions.label: Log it in the lost property register and lock it away
actions.finding: LP-0412 entered: description, found 03:50 by O. Tremlett by the lobby sofa, owner identified (room 1108), contents described by the owner, not opened, collection arranged for Friday. Locked in the front office safe.
actions.custody: Holdall LP-0412 moved from the lobby by you with O. Tremlett at {time} and locked in the front office safe.

actions.label: Brief the night manager
actions.finding: Felix Amadi notes it for the morning handover and asks the bell team to add a lobby sweep after the airport departures.

questions.prompt: Owen offers to carry the bag to the luggage room. What do you say?

options.label: "Thanks, Owen, leave it where it is for now. I'll take a look and check the cameras first. Keep people away from the sofa, and keep your radio at the desk while I do."
options.feedback: Nobody moves an item until it has been assessed, and radios stay back in case it is not what it seems.

reply.speaker: bell_captain
reply.text: Right you are. I'll keep folk round the other side.

options.label: "Yes please, bring it over to the desk."
options.feedback: You asked a colleague to pick up an unassessed item and walk it through the lobby. If it had been dangerous, he would have carried it to the busiest point in the building.

options.label: "Don't touch it. I'm evacuating the lobby and calling the police."
options.feedback: Safe, but you had not assessed it yet. A full evacuation for a gym bag every night is how staff stop taking real alarms seriously.

questions.prompt: Having looked at it and the cameras, what is your assessment?

options.label: Not hidden, nothing obviously suspicious, typical of the place and time, and the cameras show who left it and why. Treat it as lost property with a record.
options.feedback: A reasoned assessment against the three questions, backed by evidence. That is what makes "lost property" a safe call.

options.label: Unattended for over thirty minutes: always clear the lobby and call the police.
options.feedback: Time alone is not the test. If it were hidden, suspicious or untypical, yes; this one is explained by the footage.

options.label: It's obviously just luggage. No need for any of that.
options.feedback: Probably, and it was. But "obviously" is a feeling; the three questions and the footage are the assessment.

options.label: An unattended holdall in the lobby was assessed as not suspicious, its owner (departed guest, room 1108) identified on CCTV and by phone, and it was logged as lost property LP-0412.
options.feedback: Says what was found, how it was assessed and how it ended.

options.label: Suspicious package in the lobby. Resolved.
options.feedback: It was assessed as not suspicious. "Suspicious package" in a report can trigger a response that was never needed.

options.label: Bag found, given to the desk.
options.feedback: It leaves out the assessment, which is the part that protects you if anyone asks later.

questions.prompt: Incident report, which of these belong in the findings?

options.label: Found 03:50 by O. Tremlett beside the lobby sofa; no Veldane luggage tag.
Assessed at {time:observe_bag}: in view, no wires, liquid, smell or sound; typical of early departures.
CCTV L-04: left by the 03:21 departure (room 1108) at 03:27.
Owner confirmed the bag and contents by phone; not opened.

checks.label: Hear the person who found it
checks.pass: Owen told you when he found it and that it was never tagged in.
checks.fail: You never asked the person who found it.

checks.label: Assess before touching
checks.pass: You assessed the bag from a distance before anyone touched it.
checks.fail: The bag was moved before it was assessed.

checks.label: Never open an unassessed item
checks.pass: Nobody opened it. The owner described the contents instead.
checks.fail: You opened an unattended item in a public lobby before you knew what it was.

checks.label: Cameras before moving it
checks.pass: The footage explained the bag before it was moved: who, when and why.
checks.fail: You moved it without knowing how it got there.

checks.label: Find the owner
checks.pass: The owner knows where his bag is and how to get it back.
checks.fail: The owner was identified but never told.

checks.label: Record the property
checks.pass: Logged with who found it, who moved it, and where it is.
checks.fail: No lost property record: if the bag goes missing again, nobody can say where it went.

checks.label: Brief the night manager
checks.pass: The night manager knows and has added a lobby sweep after departures.

checks.label: Resolve it promptly
checks.pass: Assessed, explained and logged within the hour.
checks.fail: It took too long: a lobby item left an hour is an item people start to worry about.

debrief.whatHappened: A trade fair delegate left his gym bag by the sofa when his taxi came. It was harmless, and the night was quiet because you treated it as an unknown until the evidence said otherwise: nobody touched it, nobody opened it, and the cameras and the desk explained it in twenty minutes.
bestPractice: Ask who found it, when, and whether anyone touched it.
Assess from a distance: is it hidden, obviously suspicious, or untypical for the place? Do not touch, move or open it.
Keep radios and phones a safe distance from an item you have not assessed.
Use CCTV and the front office to find who left it and why.
If it is hidden, suspicious or unexplained: clear the area, keep people back, call the police and follow the bomb threat and evacuation plan.
If it is typical and explained: treat it as lost property with a witness, a tag and a register entry.
Contact the owner; let them describe the contents rather than opening it.
debrief.why: Most unattended bags are forgotten luggage, and that is exactly why they are dangerous to handle casually. The assessment protects the guests if it is real, and protects the hotel from needless evacuations and from "you went through my bag" complaints if it is not.
commonMistakes: Carrying it to the desk to "get it out of the way".
Opening it to find a name.
Using a radio right beside it.
Evacuating on time alone, without an assessment.

lesson: Assess before you touch: hidden, obviously suspicious, typical? Then let the evidence decide.
